extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and developers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation listing gp/PARI default configuration options (defaults/toggles), their meanings, examples, caveats, and the semantics of standard monadic/dyadic operators in gp. Intended as a precise specification for using and configuring PARI/GP and for understanding operator behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: colors
rubrics_metrics.description: Default colors string controlling colors used for various output objects (error messages, history numbers, prompt, input line, output, help messages, timer). Accepted values are strings "a1,...,ak" where k ≤ 7 and each ai is either the keyword no, an integer between 0 and 15 (colormap index), or a triple [c0,c1,c2] (foreground, background, attributes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If k < 7, remaining ai are assumed to be no. Example: default(colors, "9, 5, no, no, 4") typesets error messages in color 9, history numbers in color 5, output in color 4. Special presets: darkbg, lightbg (abbreviations allowed, e.g. d) and boldfg. EMACS: this default is incompatible with PariEmacs (change will fail silently); customize from PariEmacs side. Default value is "" (no colors). See misc/color.dft for example.

rubrics_metrics.name: compatible
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility default; marked obsolete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This default is now a no-op.

rubrics_metrics.name: datadir
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of directory containing optional data files (e.g., elldata, galdata, galpol, seadata packages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is /usr/local/share/pari, or the override specified via Configure --datadir=.

rubrics_metrics.name: debug
rubrics_metrics.description: Debugging level toggle: if non-zero, gp may print extra debugging messages according to context (see \g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0 (no debugging messages).

rubrics_metrics.name: debugfiles
rubrics_metrics.description: File usage debugging level: if non-zero, gp prints information on file descriptors in use (see \gf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0 (no debugging messages).

rubrics_metrics.name: debugmem
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory debugging level. If non-zero, gp prints notifications about memory use at increasing verbosity depending on the numeric level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior: debugmem > 0: notify when parisize changes; >1: indicate important garbage collection and the function it occurs in; >2: indicate creation/destruction of blocks (expect lots of messages). Important: on a version compiled for debugging and debugmem > 1, gp will regularly print stack usage changes by 1 MByte; this is disabled on non-debugging builds as it slows performance. Default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: echo
rubrics_metrics.description: Echo mode: 0 (off), 1 (on), 2 (on, raw). When on, each command is reprinted before execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usefulness: reading files with \r or read. echo=1 cleans input (removes whitespace/comments and unites multi-line input). echo=2 (raw) writes input as-is without preprocessing. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor add primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). When on, integer factorization machinery calls addprimes on prime factors that were difficult to find (larger than 2^24), so they are automatically tried first in other factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantage: recover prime factors already found if factorization was interrupted. Downside: huge addprimes table unrelated to current computations will slow down arithmetic functions relying on integer factorization; then use removeprimes to empty the table. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor proven
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). When set, factors output by integer factorization machinery are primality-proven rather than pseudo-primes; results depending on factorization become fully proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not affect explicit partial factorization requests or the private addprimes table (entries included as-is without testing). Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: format
rubrics_metrics.description: Printing format for real numbers of the form x.n where x ∈ {e,f,g} determines conversion style and n is precision (integer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Styles: 'e' scientific with explicit exponent; 'f' fixed-point without exponent (large real numbers with poorly defined integer part printed in e); 'g' prints in f except when decimal exponent < -4 then e; zero printed in e. Precision n is number of significant digits printed, except n < 0 prints all significant digits. Initial defaults: g.28 (32-bit) and g.38 (64-bit). For more formatting, see printf and Strprintf.

rubrics_metrics.name: graphcolormap
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector of colors used by hi-res graphing routines; length arbitrary but must contain at least 3 entries (background, frame/ticks, axes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colors may be names (restricted to lowercase and no whitespace) or RGB codes: [r,g,b] with integers 0–255, or '#RRGGBB'. Example: [250,235,215], "#faebd7", and "antiquewhite" are equivalent. Default: ["white","black","blue","violetred","red","green","grey","gainsboro"].

rubrics_metrics.name: graphcolors
rubrics_metrics.description: Indices of entries in graphcolormap used to plot multi-curves; successive curves are drawn in graphcolormap[graphcolors[1]], graphcolormap[graphcolors[2]], ... cycling when exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is [4,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: help
rubrics_metrics.description: Name/path of the external help program to use from within gp when extended help is invoked (?? or ??? or M-H under readline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is the path to the gphelp script installed with PARI.

rubrics_metrics.name: histfile
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of a file where gp will keep a history of all input commands (results omitted). If this file exists when histfile changes, it is read in and becomes part of the session history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting this default in your gprc saves readline history between sessions. Setting to empty string "" changes it to <undefined>. By default number of history entries saved is not limited; set history-size in readline's .inputrc to limit file size. Default is <undefined> (no history file).

rubrics_metrics.name: histsize
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of past results gp keeps (accessible via % notation); when exceeded oldest values are erased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tampering with this default is the only way to remove old results. Default value is 5000.

rubrics_metrics.name: lines
rubrics_metrics.description: If set to a positive value, gp prints at most that many lines from each result, terminating the last line shown with [+++] if further material has been suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various print commands are unaffected, so print(%) or \a can view the full result. If screen width cannot be determined, a 'line' is assumed to be 80 characters. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: linewrap
rubrics_metrics.description: If set to a positive value, gp wraps every single line after printing that many characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0 (unset).

rubrics_metrics.name: log
rubrics_metrics.description: Logging mode: 0 (off), 1, 2, 3 (on with modes). When on, gp opens a log file and writes commands and results to it (name determined by logfile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modes: 1 = plain logfile; 2 = emit color codes to logfile (if colors set); 3 = write LaTeX output to logfile (customizable via TeXstyle). If a file with the same name exists, gp appends. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: logfile
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of the log file used when log toggle is on; environment and time expansion are performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is "pari.log".

rubrics_metrics.name: nbthreads
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of threads to use for parallel computing in parallel builds of PARI/gp (Configure --mt=prthread or mpi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaning depends on mt engine: 'single' not used (always single thread); 'pthread' is number of threads (unlimited, default: number of cores); 'mpi' is number of MPI processes to use (limited to number allocated by mpirun, default: use all allocated processes). See also threadsize and threadsizemax. Ignored in non-parallel builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: new galois format
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If on, polgalois will use a different, more consistent naming scheme for Galois groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided so scripts can control behavior and avoid breakage. Default is 0; value will change to 1 in the next major version.

rubrics_metrics.name: output
rubrics_metrics.description: Output printing mode with three values: 0 (raw), 1 (prettymatrix), 3 (external prettyprint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: raw prints equivalent to input (allows easy copy/paste); prettymatrix prints matrices as boxes (prettier but takes more space and non-input); external prettyprint pipes gp output in TeX format to external prettyprinter (according to prettyprinter). Objects can be printed in any format at any time using \a, \m, and \B respectively. Default is 1 (prettymatrix).

rubrics_metrics.name: parisize
rubrics_metrics.description: Stack size (in bytes) gp and programs using PARI library use for computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to increase this default in gprc to match typical computations. Also set parisizemax to a much larger value so PARI can grow the stack if needed (up to parisizemax) and restore to original parisize after heavy computations. Default value is 4M (32-bit) or 8M (64-bit).

rubrics_metrics.name: parisizemax
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum size (in bytes) the stack can grow to if non-zero; if zero, the stack is limited to parisize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When set, PARI tries to fit computations within parisize but will increase roughly doubling each time up to parisizemax and print a message when increasing. After computation it restores parisize. Strongly recommended to set permanently to a large non-zero value in gprc. Can be changed inside a running gp session via default. Default value is 0 (for backward compatibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: path
rubrics_metrics.description: List of directories (':'-separated on UNIX, ';' on DOS/Windows) where gp looks for files when a non-absolute path is given; '.' means current dir and '..' parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment expansion is performed. Defaults: ".:~:~/gp" on UNIX, ".;C:\;C:\GP" on DOS/OS2/Windows, and "." otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: plothsizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Array containing plot terminal size parameters if graphic driver allows it: size of terminal, font size, tick size.

rubrics_metrics.name: prettyprinter
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of an external prettyprinter to use when output = 3 (alternate prettyprinter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is "tex2mail -TeX -noindent -ragged -by par". Note default tex2mail looks much nicer than built-in beautified format (output = 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: primelimit
rubrics_metrics.description: Value up to which gp precomputes all primes at initialization; used for sieves and trial division purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Max value depends on architecture; default value is 500k. Guarantee: first 6547 primes up to 65557 are precomputed even if primelimit is 1. This default is only used on startup (changing it does not recompute a new table). Deprecated usage notes: some algebraic number theory functions used primelimit (deprecated), and factor(N,0) partial factoring by primelimit is deprecated—use factor(N,bound).

rubrics_metrics.name: prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt string printed by gp; accepts usual escape sequences (\e, \n, \\), and is sent through strftime for time constructs (e.g. %H, %M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using readline, escape sequences can cause display bugs; bracing them with \[ and \] (if supported) avoids issues. PariEmacs needs to know prompt pattern to separate input and output; adapting automatically to arbitrary prompts is non-trivial—see PariEmacs docs. Default value shown as "?\n".

rubrics_metrics.name: prompt cont
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt string printed for continuation lines (e.g., between braces or after line-terminating backslash).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everything that applies to prompt applies to prompt cont as well. Default value is "".

rubrics_metrics.name: psfile
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete default for PostScript file output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plotexport, plothexport or plothrawexport functions and write result to file instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: readline
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch to enable or disable readline line-editing facilities inside gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn off if gp is run in environments that interact badly with readline (e.g., Sun cmdtool). When disabled advanced editing features like automatic completion and editing history are not available. Default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: realbitprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of significant bits used to convert exact inputs to transcendental functions or to create absolute floating point constants; also relates to internal precision for printing t_REAL (format may override printed digits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most PARI functions handle precision on a word basis (increments of 32 or 64 bits) so bit precision may be larger than expected. Example: to get 10 bits need one word on 64-bit => 64 bits; conversion to decimal digits: 64 bits ≈ 19 printed digits. The value shown by default(realbitprecision) is internal bits. Example session demonstrates mapping between realbitprecision and realprecision. Default value is 128 (64-bit) and 96 (32-bit).

rubrics_metrics.name: realprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of significant digits used to convert exact inputs to transcendental functions or create absolute floating point constants; also used for printing t_REAL unless overridden by format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PARI internal precision works on a word basis so may be larger than expected (one word on 64-bit gives 19 digits). default(realprecision) returns internal number of significant digits, not printed digits. Example: default(realprecision,2) shows internal 19 significant digits (2 displayed). Default value is 38 (64-bit) and 28 (32-bit).

rubrics_metrics.name: recover
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If set to 0, any error becomes fatal and causes gp interpreter to exit immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful in batch job scripts. Default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: secure
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If on, the system and extern commands are disabled to prevent execution of arbitrary UNIX commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gp will ask for confirmation before letting a script unset this toggle. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: seriesprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of significant terms when converting a polynomial or rational function to a power series (see \ps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). When on, PARI library does certain automatic type simplifications (rational to integer when exact, rational functions to polynomials when equal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only some automatic conversions are done; disabling can be useful. When off, use simplify function explicitly to simplify objects recursively (see \y). Default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: sopath
rubrics_metrics.description: List of directories where gp looks for shared libraries when installing an external symbol by name (':'-separated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When name not absolute, gp looks in these directories in order. '.' and '..' behave as usual. Environment expansion is performed. Default value is "" (empty list): install will use library name as input and look in current directory if name not absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: strictargs
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If on, all arguments to new user functions are mandatory unless the function supplies an explicit default value; otherwise arguments default to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fun(a,b=2)=a+b; with strictargs on, fun() triggers missing mandatory argument 'a'. This applies to functions defined while strictargs is on; changing strictargs does not affect previously defined functions. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: strictmatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle previously present; now obsolete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This toggle is now a no-op.

rubrics_metrics.name: threadsize
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-thread private stack size in bytes for parallel PARI/gp; ignored in non-parallel builds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total memory allocated ≈ parisize + nbthreads × threadsize. If set to 0, value used is same as parisize. Hard to estimate; recommended not to set unless solving specific problem. If warnings about not enough memory for new thread stack appear, threadsize may need increase. Recommend also setting parisizemax and threadsizemax non-zero. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: threadsizemax
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-thread maximal stack size in bytes for parallel PARI/gp; ignored in non-parallel builds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total memory allocated will be between parisize + nbthreads × threadsize and parisizemax + nbthreads × threadsizemax. If set to 0, value used is same as threadsize. Strong recommendation to set both parisizemax and threadsizemax to non-zero values. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: timer
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). When on, every instruction sequence in gp is timed and the timing is printed immediately before the output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed time is user CPU time, not including printing time. Times < 1 ms produce no printing (so defining a function, alias or installing a symbol does not print). Example: ? factor(2^2^7+1) prints 'time = 108 ms.' before output. See # and ##. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monadic + and - (+/-)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monadic operators: +x does nothing; -x negates x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gneg(GEN x) for -x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition (+)
rubrics_metrics.description: x + y is the sum of x and y. Addition between scalar x and t_COL or t_MAT y returns respectively [y[1] + x, y[2], ...] and y + xId. Other additions between scalar and vector/matrix, or between vectors/matrices of incompatible sizes are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gadd(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtraction (-)
rubrics_metrics.description: x - y is the difference of x and y. Subtraction between scalar x and t_COL or t_MAT y returns [y[1] − x, y[2], ...] and y − xId. Other subtractions between scalar and vector/matrix, or incompatible sizes are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gsub(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication (*)
rubrics_metrics.description: x * y is the product. Multiplication is not generally commutative because of vector/matrix operations; restricted to scalars it is commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbidden: multiplication between vectors/matrices of incompatible sizes, between two t_VECs or two t_COLs (use transpose for scalar product). Special behaviors: compose binary quadratic forms; compose t_VECSMALL permutations. Library syntax: GEN gmul(GEN x, GEN y); GEN gsqr(GEN x) for x*x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division (/)
rubrics_metrics.description: x / y is the quotient; result is as exact as possible. Division of two integers yields a rational number (not Euclidean quotient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If divisor is a matrix it must be invertible square matrix; result x*y^{-1}. For approximate real value of integer quotient add 0.; for p-adic quotient add O(p^k); for Taylor expansion add O(X^k) or use taylor. Library syntax: GEN gdiv(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclidean quotient (\)
rubrics_metrics.description: x \ y is the Euclidean quotient: floor(x/y) if y>0, ceil(x/y) if y<0 when division not exact; remainder x - (x\y)*y is in [0,|y|[.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When y is integer and x polynomial, y promoted to degree 0 polynomial. Applied componentwise to vectors and matrices. Library syntax: GEN gdivent(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounded Euclidean quotient (\/)
rubrics_metrics.description: x \/ y is the rounded Euclidean quotient: quotient chosen so remainder is smallest in absolute value; in tie choose quotient closest to +∞, remainder in ]−|y|/2,|y|/2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied componentwise. Library syntax: GEN gdivround(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular remainder (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: x % y evaluates the modular Euclidean remainder. For non-integral reals, x%y = x - (x\y)*y. If y integer, return smallest non-negative integer congruent to x mod y. If y polynomial, return polynomial of smallest degree congruent to x mod y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When y integer and x polynomial, y promoted to degree 0 polynomial. Applied componentwise. Examples illustrate subtle differences between (1/2) % 3 and 0.5 % 3. Library syntax: GEN gmod(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Powering (^)
rubrics_metrics.description: x^n is powering. If n integer use exact binary powering; if exponent non-integer use exp(n log x) acting componentwise; special cases for rational p/q exponents on Mod or p-adics; negative integer exponent computes inverse and may fail on non-invertible objects (revealing a factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Powering rewrites x*x as x2 when operands are identical labels (same memory). For integer exponents powering is exact; for rational exponents on modular or p-adic contexts returns roots if exist (q must not have large prime factors). Negative exponent behavior can reveal nontrivial factors of modulus when inverse impossible. For t_MAT exponent expects square invertible matrix except x^{-1} returns left inverse for full column rank rectangular x. Library syntax: GEN gpow(GEN x, GEN n, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: cmp(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal comparison returning -1, 0, or 1. Underlying order is transitive; returns 0 iff x === y (identical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing same types: integers compare as usual; t_VECSMALL compare lexicographically; t_STR lexicographic. If components equal up to smallest length, the more complex (longer) is larger; when lengths equal matrix > vector > scalar. Use cmp for sorting arbitrary objects (vecsort(v, cmp) ≡ Set(v)). Library syntax: GEN cmp_universal(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: divrem(x,y,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns column vector [Euclidean quotient (x\y), Euclidean remainder (x - (x\y)*y)]. If v present and polynomials multivariate, divide w.r.t variable v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids doing two divisions separately. Beware: divrem(x,y)[2] is in general not the same as x%y (examples shown). Library syntax: GEN divrem(GEN x, GEN y, long v = -1). Also GEN gdiventres(GEN x, GEN y) when v not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: lex(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexicographic comparison returning -1,0,1. Accepts comparisons between objects of different types (scalars, vectors, matrices) recursively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When components equal up to smallest length, longer is larger; when lengths equal, matrix > vector > scalar. Examples illustrate behavior with nested vectors and transposes. Library syntax: GEN lexcmp(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: max(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the maximum of x and y when they can be compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gmax(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: min(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the minimum of x and y when they can be compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gmin(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: powers(x,n,{x0})
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-negative n, returns vector [1, x, ..., x^n] if x0 omitted, else [x0, x0*x, ..., x0*x^n].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: powers(Mod(3,17),4) etc. When n < 0 returns empty vector []. Library syntax: GEN gpowers0(GEN x, long n, GEN x0 = NULL) and GEN gpowers(GEN x, long n) when x0 NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: shift(x,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shifts x componentwise left by n bits if n ≥ 0 and right by |n| bits if n < 0. Abbreviations: x << n or x >> (-n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Left shift by n corresponds to multiplication by 2^n. Right shift of integer x by |n| corresponds to Euclidean division by 2^{|n|} with remainder of same sign as x (not same as x\2^n necessarily). Library syntax: GEN gshift(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: shiftmul(x,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplies x by 2^n. Differs from shift when n < 0: shift uses Euclidean division (integers remain integers), shiftmul uses ordinary division (may produce fractions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gmul2n(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: sign(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns sign of x (0, 1, or -1) for integer, real, or fraction types; supports t_QUAD with positive discriminants and t_INFINITY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gsigne(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecmax(x,{&v})
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is vector or matrix, returns largest entry; otherwise returns a copy of x. Error if x empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If v is given, set it to index (or coordinates [i,j]) of a largest entry. Examples provided. Library syntax: GEN vecmax0(GEN x, GEN *v = NULL) and GEN vecmax(GEN x) when v not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: vecmin(x,{&v})
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is vector or matrix, returns smallest entry; otherwise returns a copy of x. Error if x empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If v given, set it to index (or coordinates) of smallest entry. Examples provided. Library syntax: GEN vecmin0(GEN x, GEN *v = NULL) and GEN vecmin(GEN x) when v not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison and Boolean operators (<=,<,>=,>,==,!=,===)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard comparison operators return 1 if true, 0 if false. Operator == is liberal (e.g., integer 0, 0 polynomial, and vector with 0 entries test equal). Operator === tests strict identity (objects of different type or length are never identical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use === when strict identity is required; be aware of == liberal equality semantics across types.
